fullText.simplified:
第2章、作家的第一封信

    两个多月后，李河在外面遇到了小九。小九问他那本小说怎么样。
    李河回答说：“《天花板上的客人》讲了一个很特别的故事。坏人为了杀一个有钱的女孩，在她家的天花板上住了一个月，没有被人发现。最后坏人杀了女孩，警察没有抓到他。坏人拿着女孩的钱，在国外开心地活到了八十多岁。我不喜欢这个故事，我觉得作者春草把警察写得太笨了，还是像小孩子的游戏。看完《天花板上的客人》，我又去看了春草的其他小说，结果都差不多，警察永远抓不到坏人，这太让人失望了。为什么坏人就不能被抓到呢？在作者春草心中，他真的觉得警察和他书里说的一样没用吗？”
    小九觉得李河的回答很有趣，就把这些话都发表在了最新一期的报纸上，这份报道的名字叫“优秀警察李河对著名作家春草的意见”。李河看到了这份报道，他笑了笑，没有放在心上。但是没有想到，一个星期后，他收到了一封信，写信的人就是作家春草。
    信是用打印机打印的，信的内容是这样的：

李河先生：
    您好！抱歉打扰您，我是《天花板上的客人》的作者春草。在报纸上看到了您对《天花板上的客人》的意见的报道。您是一位非常优秀的警察，大家都很喜欢您。您对侦探小说家的批评，我都知道了。虽然不同意您说的《天花板上的客人》像小孩子的游戏，但还是很高兴这本书能被您看到。
    关于您问我的问题——“在作者春草心中，他真的觉得警察和他书里说的一样没用吗？”，我已有答案。虽然我可以现在就在信中把答案告诉您，但还是觉得见面说会礼貌一些。请问您下个礼拜天下午三点有空吗？如果方便，您能来友好北路的“友好咖啡馆”吗？我会在那儿等您。
    祝您工作顺利！
春草
2月18日

    信封上只有李河的名字和地址，寄信人那儿一个字也没有，春草没有留自己的地址或电话。虽然他问李河能不能去，但他没有给李河回答的机会。看来不管有没有空，只要李河想见他，都要在下个礼拜天下午三点去“友好咖啡馆”了。
    这有点儿奇怪。因为，不管是礼貌的原因，还是为了方便联系，正常人都会留下自己的电话号码或地址，但是春草一个都没留下。更重要的是，现在谁还寄信呢？打电话、发邮件或者发手机信息，哪一个不比寄信快呢？这封打印的信真的是大作家春草写的吗？还是有人和自己开玩笑呢？
    李河心想，好吧，不管是不是玩笑，去看看就知道了。
fullText.traditional:
第2章、作家的第一封信

    兩個多月後，李河在外面遇到了小九。小九問他那本小說怎麼樣。
    李河回答說：“《天花板上的客人》講了一個很特別的故事。壞人為了殺一個有錢的女孩，在她家的天花板上住了一個月，沒有被人發現。最後壞人殺了女孩，警察沒有抓到他。壞人拿著女孩的錢，在國外開心地活到了八十多歲。我不喜歡這個故事，我覺得作者春草把警察寫得太笨了，還是像小孩子的遊戲。看完《天花板上的客人》，我又去看了春草的其他小說，結果都差不多，警察永遠抓不到壞人，這太讓人失望了。為什麼壞人就不能被抓到呢？在作者春草心中，他真的覺得警察和他書裡說的一樣沒用嗎？”
    小九覺得李河的回答很有趣，就把這些話都發表在了最新一期的報紙上，這份報道的名字叫“優秀警察李河對著名作家春草的意見”。李河看到了這份報道，他笑了笑，沒有放在心上。但是沒有想到，一個星期後，他收到了一封信，寫信的人就是作家春草。
    信是用打印機打印的，信的內容是這樣的：

李河先生：
    您好！抱歉打擾您，我是《天花板上的客人》的作者春草。在報紙上看到了您對《天花板上的客人》的意見的報道。您是一位非常優秀的警察，大家都很喜歡您。您對偵探小說家的批評，我都知道了。雖然不同意您說的《天花板上的客人》像小孩子的遊戲，但還是很高興這本書能被您看到。
    關於您問我的問題——“在作者春草心中，他真的覺得警察和他書裡說的一樣沒用嗎？”，我已有答案。雖然我可以現在就在信中把答案告訴您，但還是覺得見面說會禮貌一些。請問您下個禮拜天下午三點有空嗎？如果方便，您能來友好北路的“友好咖啡館”嗎？我會在那兒等您。
    祝您工作順利！
春草
2月18日

    信封上只有李河的名字和地址，寄信人那兒一個字也沒有，春草沒有留自己的地址或電話。雖然他問李河能不能去，但他沒有給李河回答的機會。看來不管有沒有空，只要李河想見他，都要在下個禮拜天下午三點去“友好咖啡館”了。
    這有點兒奇怪。因為，不管是禮貌的原因，還是為了方便聯繫，正常人都會留下自己的電話號碼或地址，但是春草一個都沒留下。更重要的是，現在誰還寄信呢？打電話、發郵件或者發手機信息，哪一個不比寄信快呢？這封打印的信真的是大作家春草寫的嗎？還是有人和自己開玩笑呢？
    李河心想，好吧，不管是不是玩笑，去看看就知道了。

sentences.pinyin: zhǐ yào lǐ hé xiǎng jiàn tā dōu yào zài xià ge lǐ bài tiān xià wǔ sān diǎn qù yǒu hǎo kā fēi guǎn le
sentences.english: .. if Li He wanted to see him, he must go to the Youhao Cafe at 3 o’clock in the afternoon the following Sunday.

sentences.simplified: 这有点儿奇怪。
sentences.traditional: 這有點兒奇怪。
sentences.pinyin: zhè yǒu diǎn'r qí guài
sentences.english: This was a bit strange.

sentences.simplified: 因为，不管是礼貌的原因，还是为了方便联系，
sentences.traditional: 因為，不管是禮貌的原因，還是為了方便聯繫，
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi bù guǎn shì lǐ mào de yuán yīn hái shi wèi le fāng biàn lián xì
sentences.english: Because, whether it was for reasons of politeness or to make it easy to get in touch, ..

sentences.simplified: 正常人都会留下自己的电话号码或地址，但是春草一个都没留下。
sentences.traditional: 正常人都會留下自己的電話號碼或地址，但是春草一個都沒留下。
sentences.pinyin: zhèng cháng rén dōu huì liú xià zì jǐ de diàn huà hào mǎ huò dì zhǐ dàn shì chūn cǎo yí ge dōu méi liú xià
sentences.english: .. normal people would leave their own phone number or address, but Chun Cao did not leave any of those.

sentences.simplified: 更重要的是，现在谁还寄信呢？
sentences.traditional: 更重要的是，現在誰還寄信呢？
sentences.pinyin: gèng zhòng yào de shì xiàn zài shéi hái jì xìn ne
sentences.english: More importantly, who still sends letters nowadays?

sentences.simplified: 打电话、发邮件或者发手机信息，哪一个不比寄信快呢？
sentences.traditional: 打電話、發郵件或者發手機信息，哪一個不比寄信快呢？
sentences.pinyin: dǎ diàn huà fā yóu jiàn huò zhě fā shǒu jī xìn xī něi yí ge bù bǐ jì xìn kuài ne
sentences.english: Calling, sending emails, or sending text messages, aren’t they all faster than sending a letter?

sentences.simplified: 这封打印的信真的是大作家春草写的吗？还是有人和自己开玩笑呢？
sentences.traditional: 這封打印的信真的是大作家春草寫的嗎？還是有人和自己開玩笑呢？
sentences.pinyin: zhè fēng dǎ yìn de xìn zhēn de shì dà zuò jiā chūn cǎo xiě de ma hái shi yǒu rén hé zì jǐ kāi wán xiào ne
sentences.english: Was this printed letter really written by the great author Chun Cao? Or was someone joking with him?

sentences.simplified: 李河心想，好吧，不管是不是玩笑，去看看就知道了。
sentences.traditional: 李河心想，好吧，不管是不是玩笑，去看看就知道了。
sentences.pinyin: lǐ hé xīn xiǎng hǎo ba bù guǎn shì bú shì wán xiào qù kàn kan jiù zhī dào le
sentences.english: Li He thought to himself: Okay, whether it’s a joke or not, I’ll go and take a look.

sentence_translations: Chapter 2: The Author’s First Letter
More than two months later, Li He ran into Xiaojiu outside. Xiaojiu asked him what he thought about the novel.
Li He replied, “The Guest in the Ceiling tells a very unusual story.
In order to kill a rich girl, the bad guy lived in the ceiling of her house for a month without being discovered.
In the end, the bad guy killed the girl, and the police didn’t catch him.
The bad guy took the girl’s money and lived happily abroad until he was more than 80 years old.
I don’t like this story. I think the author Chun Cao made the police look too stupid. It is like a child’s game.
After reading The Guest in the Ceiling, I also read Chun Cao’s other novels, and they had similar endings.
The police could never catch the bad guys. This was so disappointing. Why can’t the bad guys be caught?
In his mind, does the author Chun Cao really think that the police are as useless as he says in his books?”
Xiaojiu found Li He’s answer very interesting, so he published what he said in the latest issue of the newspaper.
The name of this report was “The Outstanding Police Officer Li He’s Opinions on the Famous Author Chun Cao”.
When Li He saw the report, he smiled and didn’t take it seriously.
But he did not expect that a week later, he would receive a letter. The writer of the letter was the author Chun Cao.
The letter was printed out using a printer, and the content of the letter was as follows:
Mr. Li He:
Hello! Sorry to bother you. I am Chun Cao, the author of The Guest in the Ceiling.
I saw the report on your opinion of The Guest in the Ceiling in the newspaper.
You are an outstanding police officer, and everyone likes you very much.
I know about your criticism of detective novelists.
Although I do not agree with what you said about The Guest in the Ceiling being like a child’s game, ..
.. I am still very glad that this book could be read by you.
Regarding the question you asked me: “In the author Chun Cao’s mind, ..
.. does he really think that the police are as useless as he says in his books?” I have an answer.
Although I could tell you the answer in this letter right now, I still think it would be more polite to meet.
Are you free at 3 o’clock in the afternoon next Sunday?
If it is convenient, can you come to the Youhao Cafe on Youhao North Road? I will wait for you there.
I wish you success in your work!
Chun Cao
February 18
Only Li He’s name and address were on the envelope.
There was not a single word about the sender, and Chun Cao hadn’t left his own address or phone number.
Although he asked Li He if he could go, he hadn’t given Li He a chance to answer.
It seemed that no matter whether he was free or not, ..
.. if Li He wanted to see him, he must go to the Youhao Cafe at 3 o’clock in the afternoon the following Sunday.
This was a bit strange.
Because, whether it was for reasons of politeness or to make it easy to get in touch, ..
.. normal people would leave their own phone number or address, but Chun Cao did not leave any of those.
More importantly, who still sends letters nowadays?
Calling, sending emails, or sending text messages, aren’t they all faster than sending a letter?
Was this printed letter really written by the great author Chun Cao? Or was someone joking with him?
Li He thought to himself: Okay, whether it’s a joke or not, I’ll go and take a look.
